verdictDetail: The wine-on-aarch64 path is fully validated; the application itself never creates a window. Every architectural claim under test passed. Slack fails for reasons internal to its own Windows-API assumptions.
backendDetail: wineWow64Packages.stable (wine-wow64-11.0). NO emulation: box64, FEX and muvm are all absent from this package.

payload.formatNote: The ARM64 Windows build is MSIX-ONLY; there is no SlackSetup.exe for arm64 (verified: x64 has both SlackSetup.exe and Slack.msix, arm64 has only the .msix). wine has no AppX/MSIX deployment stack, so the package is extracted rather than installed — MSIX is a plain ZIP with compression method=store.
payload.peMachineNote: Asserted at build time. A silent flip to 0x8664 would void the no-emulation premise, so the build fails loudly instead.

proven: PLAN2 §2 (route table) row 3 — an ARM64 Windows PE runs under plain wine on aarch64 with zero emulation. This row was previously marked (unverified).
The non-credentialed fetch path: plain fetchurl with a pinned hash, no sandbox-path grant, no credential store.
MSIX extract-and-run as a workaround for wine's missing AppX stack.
PLAN2 §7.2 state layout: $XDG_STATE_HOME/propnix/<app>/ for the prefix, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR for ephemera.
The prefix stamp keyed on the wine store path: wineboot -u runs once, not on every launch.
Prefix setup with DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY unset suppresses wine's 'configuration is being updated' dialog entirely (user-confirmed absent).

notWorking.symptom: No window is ever created. Electron initialises fully, spawns 9 renderer processes and composites a 1200x998 framebuffer, but produces ZERO X11 toplevels and nothing visible under Wayland either.
notWorking.isolation: wine presents windows correctly on this host under BOTH drivers — wine's own notepad produced a visible window under wayland AND under x11 (both user-confirmed). Slack fails under both. Therefore the fault is neither wine's display layer nor the driver choice.
notWorking.likelyCause: Slack's own startup code throws before window creation: `isElectronDebugLoggingSupported: Failed when attempting to detect mount point in log path — TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'isMountPoint')`. Also `WSALookupServiceBegin failed with: 8`. Both are Windows-API surfaces wine does not expose as Slack expects.
notWorking.notPursued: Diagnosing further means reverse-engineering a minified Electron bundle. Poor value for a proof of concept whose architectural questions are already answered.

gameArgs.reason: Electron's GPU CHILD process cannot launch under wine (`GPU process launch failed: error_code=40` then `GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.`). --in-process-gpu folds it into the main process and clears the error.

WINEDLLOVERRIDES.reason: suppresses the .NET and Gecko install prompts

Graphics.reason: wineWow64 ships winewayland.drv for aarch64-windows. Driver choice is a runtime registry setting, not a package choice. Wayland is verified working on this host, so there is no reason to prefer x11.

measuredAlternatives.--disable-gpu-sandbox alone: insufficient — GPU process still failed to launch
measuredAlternatives.--disable-gpu: traded the GPU-process error for `DCompositionCreateDevice3 failed: Not implemented` and exit code 5. The blunter fix was worse; keeping acceleration on and avoiding the child process is correct.
measuredAlternatives.--disable-gpu --disable-gpu-compositing: no GPU error, but still no window
measuredAlternatives.Graphics=x11 instead of wayland: no change to the Slack outcome — which is what proves the driver is not the variable

correctionsToPlan: The flock single-instance guard is Unity/box64-specific, NOT a universal wrapper feature. `wineserver` lingers by design and inherits the lock fd, so it kept holding the lock after Slack exited and refused the next launch. Electron implements single-instance itself.

A wine wrapper's exit code is not meaningful: Slack detaches, so the wrapper returns 0 while the app keeps running. A real wrapper must either wait on wineserver or document that it returns immediately.

Wine's Wayland driver presents correctly here. An earlier draft of this record concluded 'prefer x11' — that was wrong, drawn from testing notepad only after switching to x11, i.e. an incomplete matrix.
notMeasured: whether Slack works at all under wine on any architecture, including x86_64 — the x64 build was never tried, so 'ARM64 is the problem' is NOT established
whether a newer or older Slack version behaves differently
any performance figure — the app never rendered
